options: Speed reading and touch typing
Memorising facts word for word
Planning your learning, monitoring whether your strategies work and evaluating the results
Following the teacher's instructions exactly
questions.explain: Self-directed learners plan, monitor and evaluate their own learning.
questions.evidence: Metacognitive skills include planning your learning, monitoring whether your current learning strategies are successful, and evaluating results of your learning.

questions.q: In the learning cycle, which two tasks does planning involve?
options: Deciding what you need to learn and how you are going to learn it
Buying books and booking a room
Choosing a teacher and a course
Setting an exam date and a reward
questions.explain: Monitoring and evaluating follow planning in the cycle.
questions.evidence: Planning involves two key tasks: deciding what you need to learn, and then deciding how you are going to learn that material.

questions.q: What is a key element of self-efficacy?
options: Intelligence
Luck
Family background
Locus of control
questions.explain: Believing outcomes depend on your own actions supports persistence.
questions.evidence: A key element of self-efficacy is the concept of locus of control.

questions.q: What should you do when a goal feels too big to prepare for?
options: Give up and choose an easier goal
Develop smaller steps or tasks that you can start working on immediately
Wait until you have more time
Ask someone else to do it
questions.explain: Small, immediate steps beat waiting for the perfect moment.
questions.evidence: it’s important to develop smaller steps or tasks that can be started and worked on immediately.

options: Because teachers require them
To impress employers
Without goals we aren't sure what we're trying to accomplish or whether we are accomplishing anything
So we can avoid planning
questions.explain: Goals give direction and a way to measure progress.
questions.evidence: Without goals, we aren’t sure what we are trying to accomplish, and there is little way of knowing if we are accomplishing anything.

questions.q: Which skill may you need to protect your study time from interruption?
options: Saying 'no'
Multitasking
Studying with the TV on
Checking messages often
questions.explain: Knowing when and where you concentrate best also helps.
questions.evidence: Saying “no” is an important skill that may need to be utilized in order for you to have your study time without interruption.

questions.q: What does the forgetting curve show?
options: That memory improves with age
That we never forget what we read
That sleep has no effect on memory
How much information is forgotten quickly after it is learned
questions.explain: Reviewing material soon after learning slows forgetting.
questions.evidence: known as the forgetting curve, shows how much information is forgotten quickly after it is learned.

questions.q: Why take good notes on what you read?
options: To make the text longer
They help you quickly review the key points
To avoid reading the text
Notes are required by every course
questions.explain: Note-taking makes you identify the important content and its implications.
questions.evidence: Taking good notes helps you to quickly review the key points in the material that you have read.

questions.q: Why are soft skills also called 'transferable skills'?
options: Because they are taught in transfer programmes
Because they expire when you change jobs
Because you can carry them from job to job or profession to profession without much training
Because employers transfer them to you
questions.explain: Communication, teamwork and problem-solving stay useful as technology changes.
questions.evidence: Soft skills are sometimes also called “transferable skills” because you can easily transfer them from job to job or profession to profession without much training.

questions.q: According to the chapter, what is the most effective way to find a new job?
options: To network, network and network some more
To send the same CV to every company
To wait for recruiters to call
To apply only through job boards
questions.explain: Relationships open doors that applications alone don't.
questions.evidence: the most effective way to find a new job is to network, network, and network some more.
